name: hero-pattern-centered
title: Hero / centered type on a pattern
description: Centered, type-led hero: a huge display headline, one short sentence and one button over a fine repeating pattern on the page colour.
when: Top of a page when the message is strong enough to carry the first screen without a picture (studios, consultants, launches).

name: hero-split-right
title: Hero / split, tall image right
description: Asymmetric split hero: eyebrow, large headline, two lines of copy, a button and a quiet text link on a wide left column (two thirds); one tall portrait image on the right (one third).
when: Top of a page for a service, studio or practice with one strong photograph; the classic editorial first screen.

name: hero-split-left-overlap
title: Hero / image left, overlapping card
description: Split hero: a large image on the left and, on the right, a surface card holding eyebrow, headline, copy and button that slides over the image edge (on phones it overlaps the bottom of the image instead).
when: Top of a page for warm, friendly or product brands that want depth on the first screen; needs one strong image.

name: hero-image-scrim
title: Hero / full-bleed photo with a scrim
description: Tall full-bleed photograph (about 80% of the screen height) under a scrim in the overlay colour, with eyebrow, headline, copy, two buttons and a ruled strip of three short practical details, left-aligned in the inverse text colour.
when: Top of a page when one atmospheric photograph sells the experience (hospitality, travel, events, upscale brands).

name: hero-gradient-stats
title: Hero / gradient with floating figures
description: Split hero on a soft gradient from the page colour to the surface colour: headline, copy and button on the left; three small tilted surface cards with placeholder figures on the right, staggered so each just touches the next (straight and spaced on phones).
when: Top of a page for a product or service that can back its promise with real figures; the figures are placeholders the owner replaces with numbers they can prove, or the cards are removed.

name: hero-editorial-minimal
title: Hero / editorial headline
description: Minimal, left-aligned editorial hero: a small kicker, a very large display headline and a rule, then a short paragraph on the left and an underlined text link on the right (stacked on phones), with generous whitespace and no image or button.
when: Top of a page for writers, studios, firms and journals whose voice is the product; pairs best with a serif display font.

name: hero-bordered-cells
title: Hero / bold panel and three cells
description: Loud, left-aligned stacked hero: a huge headline inside a panel, a grid of three cells under it (an index label and one line each; one column on phones), then one button.
when: Top of a page for bold, raw or flat brands (agencies, events, products with attitude) that say three things fast.

name: hero-spec-card
title: Hero / split with a ruled spec card
description: Left-aligned split hero: a small version label in the eyebrow font (monospace where the language uses one, as tech-mono does), a tight headline, two lines of copy and a primary and a secondary button on the left; a card of ruled label/value lines on the right.
when: Top of a page for software, tools, developer products or technical services; the label and every value in the card are placeholders the owner replaces with real facts, or removes.

name: hero-product-glow
title: Hero / product shot with a glow
description: Centered product hero: eyebrow, headline, one sentence and two buttons over a soft radial glow, then a wide framed product picture (its corners follow the style kit) and a row of three short placeholder trust lines under it.
when: Top of a page for a software product or app with a screenshot to show; the screenshot and every trust line are placeholders the owner replaces (never invented customers, ratings or figures).

name: header-title-band
title: Page header / title band
description: Compact inner-page title band on the surface colour: a breadcrumb-style kicker line and the page title in a wide left column, a short summary in a narrow right column (under the title on phones), closed by a hairline along the bottom edge.
when: Top of an inner page (services, about, contact, legal) where the visitor needs to know where they are, not to be sold to again.

name: header-divider-intro
title: Page header / inverted band with a curve
description: Centered inner-page header on a band in the text colour (dark on light designs, light on dark ones): kicker, page title, a short rule and a short intro in the page colour, ending in a curved section divider that flows into the page colour below.
when: Top of an inner page that deserves a moment of emphasis (a service, a programme, a campaign page); follow it with a section on the page colour so the curve joins it.

name: header-image-band
title: Page header / photo band
description: Inner-page header on a photograph under a scrim in the overlay colour, shorter than a hero: breadcrumb-style kicker, page title and one line, left-aligned in the inverse text colour.
when: Top of an inner page that should keep the site's photographic mood (a location, a project, a service area); needs one landscape image.

name: features-bento
title: Features / bento grid of unequal tiles
description: Bento grid of five tiles in two rows of unequal spans: a large picture tile (two thirds) beside two stacked tiles (one on the accent colour), then a narrow inverted tile beside a wide one; above them a split intro (heading left, line and link right); one column on phones.
when: Benefits or features of a software product, studio or tool with one lead feature and four smaller ones; flat, technical or raw brands. Needs one picture.

name: features-zigzag
title: Features / zigzag image and text rows
description: Three alternating rows under a centred intro: a square-cornered 4:3 picture on one side and a numbered kicker, heading, two lines and a text link on the other, the picture switching sides on every row; on phones each row stacks with the picture first.
when: Feature or service detail when each point deserves its own picture (services, products, studios); calm, editorial and upscale brands. Needs three pictures.

name: list-icon-dividers
title: Features / icon list with dividers
description: A single centred column of five feature rows separated by rules, each row an icon on the left and a short heading with one muted line on the right, under a left-aligned intro; reads like a specification list.
when: Benefits or included features when there are five or more short points and no pictures (software, services, memberships); plain, technical and editorial brands.

name: checklist-two-column
title: Features / two-column checklist
description: A narrow left column with the heading and intro beside a two-column checklist of eight short items, each a plain tick icon beside one line, on the surface colour; one column on phones.
when: What is included in a service, package or membership, or a list of requirements met; every kind of brand. Keep each item to one line.

name: steps-numbered
title: Process / numbered steps
description: Three steps set as a ruled list: a short intro on a narrow left column, then on the right a stack of three steps, each a very large numeral (01, 02, 03) over a heading and one line, with a rule between steps; one column on phones.
when: How it works for a service or product with a simple three-step process (booking, onboarding, ordering); suits plain, editorial and technical brands.

name: steps-horizontal
title: Process / horizontal steps joined by a line
description: Four steps side by side under a centred intro, each a round numbered marker in the accent colour joined to the next by a horizontal rule, then a short heading and one line; two per row on tablets, one column without the rules on phones, and one button under the steps.
when: How it works for a service with four clear stages (consultation, plan, delivery, follow-up); friendly and modern brands that like round shapes.

name: timeline-vertical
title: Process / vertical timeline
description: One-sided vertical timeline: a short intro on a narrow left column and, on the right, four entries hung on a thin vertical rule with a small square marker each, every entry a small step or date label, a heading and one line; on phones the intro sits above the timeline.
when: How it works, a project plan or a short history in order (milestones, phases, a programme schedule); calm, technical or editorial brands. The labels are placeholders the owner replaces (never invented dates).

name: features-accordion-image
title: Features / accordion beside a picture
description: Two-column feature block: an eyebrow, heading and a ruled accordion of four short feature items (no boxes, a rule under each, the first open) on the left, one tall square-cornered 4:5 picture on the right; on phones the picture sits under the accordion.
when: Feature detail when each point needs a few sentences but the page must stay short (services, products, programmes); calm, editorial, technical and flat brands. Needs one picture.

name: compare-two-panels
title: Features / before and after panels
description: Old way versus new way: a left-aligned heading over two panels side by side, a plain panel with four crossed-out points on the left and an inverted panel in the text colour with four ticked points and a button on the right; stacked on phones.
when: Problem and solution, before and after, or doing it yourself versus with you (services, software, coaching); technical and upscale brands. Compare situations, never named competitors.

name: features-carousel-strip
title: Features / sliding feature strip
description: A left-aligned heading and line above a carousel strip of six feature items (an accent icon badge, a heading and one line each), three visible at a time on desktops, two on tablets and one on phones, moved with the arrows at either side.
when: Benefits when there are more features than fit in one row (apps, services, memberships); friendly, rounded and dark-glass brands.

name: stats-big-numbers
title: Stats / big numbers on an inverted band
description: An inverted band in the text colour (dark on light designs, light on dark ones): a short heading, then three very large placeholder figures across the full width, each under a rule and over a one-line label (one column on phones).
when: Credibility after the benefits, only when the owner has three figures they can prove (years, projects, response time); every figure and label is a bracketed placeholder to replace or remove, never an invented statistic.

name: proof-logo-wall
title: Proof / logo wall
description: A wall of six logos in a hairline-ruled panel (three across on desktops and tablets, two on phones), each logo centred on its own light cell so full-colour logos stay legible on light and dark designs; one short muted caption above.
when: Under the hero or before the testimonials, when the owner has client, partner or customer logos they have permission to show; every kind of brand with square or near-square corners. The six logos, their alt texts ([Logo 1 name] logo ...) and the caption are placeholders to replace one by one (never invented brands).

name: proof-press-quotes
title: Proof / press quotes in ruled columns
description: Three press mentions side by side under a left-aligned heading, each column topped by a rule: the publication name set as an uppercase text mark, a one-line quote in italics and a muted source line; one column on phones.
when: Credibility when the business has real press coverage it can quote and link to (studios, products, restaurants, authors). Every publication, quote and source is a bracketed placeholder: use only real coverage, quoted word for word, never invented.

name: proof-rating-strip
title: Proof / rating strip
description: A slim band on the surface colour with a hairline under it: on the left five star glyphs, a placeholder score and the review count with its source; on the right three short trust points, each an icon and a few words; the two halves stack on phones.
when: Right under a hero or beside a price, when the business has a public rating it can link to and a few checkable promises (shops, apps, local services). The score, count, source and trust points are placeholders: show only a real rating with its source, never an invented one.

name: stats-counter-band
title: Stats / counter band on the accent colour
description: A band in the accent colour: a heading and one line on a narrow left column, four number counters that count up on scroll in a two-by-two grid on the right, each under a thin rule with a short label; one column on phones.
when: Credibility in the middle of a page when the owner has four figures they can prove (years, projects, clients, response time); bold and confident brands. The numbers 100, 50, 25 and 10 are demo values (a counter needs a number): replace each with a figure the owner can prove, or remove it; every label says so. Never an invented statistic.

name: stats-circle-counters
title: Stats / circle counters
description: A centred heading and line above a four-column row of circle counters (a ring that fills to a percentage on scroll, the number in the middle, a short label under it), two by two on tablets and one column on phones; the ring in the accent colour on a track in the border colour.
when: Results, satisfaction or progress shown as percentages when the owner can prove each one (completion rates, repeat clients, on-time delivery); friendly, rounded and dashboard-like brands. The rings 80, 60, 40 and 20 percent are demo values (a ring needs a number): replace each with a percentage the owner can prove, or remove it; every label says so. Never invented.

name: stats-big-captions
title: Stats / big numerals with small captions
description: A split intro (heading left, one line right) over a hairline-ruled row of four cells: in each a very large, light-weight placeholder numeral and a small caption under it; four across on desktops, two by two on tablets and phones.
when: Credibility for calm, editorial or technical brands that let the numbers speak (studios, consultancies, software); the figures are bracketed placeholders to replace with numbers the owner can prove, or remove.

name: quote-single-large
title: Testimonial / one large quote
description: One oversized quote centred on a plain band: a large opening quote mark, the quote set big in the display font (up to 960px wide), then a centred attribution line with a round avatar, the name and the role.
when: One strong testimonial between sections, when a single voice says it better than a grid (coaches, studios, services); warm, friendly and trustworthy brands that allow round avatars. The quote, name, role and avatar are placeholders for a real client's words, used with permission.

name: testimonials-slider-quote
title: Testimonials / quote slider in a rounded panel
description: A heading and line on a narrow left column beside a rounded, hairline-framed panel on the surface colour that slides through three quotes, each a small attribution over a large quote in the display font, with arrows and dots; the panel goes under the heading on phones.
when: Several short testimonials in little space (services, apps, courses); friendly, rounded and dark-glass brands that like carousels. Names and quotes are placeholders for real clients' words, used with permission.

name: testimonials-avatar-grid
title: Testimonials / heading cell and three quote tiles
description: A two-by-two matrix where the first cell holds the eyebrow, heading and one line and the other three are quote tiles on the surface colour, each a quote with a small square avatar, the name and the role at the bottom; one column on phones, the heading first.
when: Three testimonials from different kinds of clients (services, B2B, agencies, clinics); calm, editorial, technical and trustworthy brands. Quotes, names, roles and avatars are placeholders for real clients' words and photos, used with permission.

name: quote-over-image
title: Testimonial / quote over a photo
description: A photo band under a dark scrim with one quote in large light type on the left (up to 760px wide), then a short light rule and the name and role under it; tall padding, no card.
when: One emotional testimonial on a page that already has a strong photo mood (hospitality, travel, wellness, architecture); every kind of brand. Needs one photo; the quote, name and role are placeholders for a real client's words.

name: pricing-three-tier
title: Pricing / three plans, the middle one highlighted
description: A centred intro over three plan cards side by side (two on the surface colour, the middle one filled with the accent colour): plan name, one line, a large price, a ruled list of three ticked features and a button; the middle plan carries a "[Most popular]" label and the primary button; one column on tablets and phones.
when: Pricing for software, memberships or packaged services with three clear levels; modern and dark-glass brands. Plan names, prices, periods, features and the label are placeholders: use the owner's real offer only.

name: pricing-two-plan-highlight
title: Pricing / two plans, one inverted
description: A heading column beside two plans: a plan on the page colour and a recommended plan in inverted colours (the text colour as its fill) with a "[Recommended]" label; each a big price, its terms, a ruled list of five ticked features and a button; the heading goes on top on tablets, the plans stack on phones.
when: Pricing with exactly two options (monthly or yearly, standard or full service, one-off or retainer); flat, technical and upscale brands. Every name, price, term and feature is a placeholder for the owner's real offer.

name: pricing-comparison-table
title: Pricing / plan comparison table
description: A left-aligned intro over a hairline-ruled comparison table built from groups: a feature column and three plan columns (name and price in the header row; ticks, dashes or a limit in each feature row), the middle plan's column tinted and labelled "[Most popular]"; the table keeps its columns on phones; one button under it.
when: Under pricing cards or on a dedicated pricing page, when plans differ by many features (software, memberships, hosting); calm, technical and upscale brands. Plan names, prices, features and limits are placeholders: fill in the owner's real plans only. Keep feature names short (phone cells are narrow) and put any meaning a tick or dash carries into words.

name: team-grid
title: Team / four portraits in a row
description: A split intro (heading left, one line right) over four square portraits in a row, each with the name under a rule and the role as a small label; two by two on tablets, one column on phones.
when: An about or team page, or trust before a contact form, when the owner can show real people (studios, agencies, clinics, firms); calm, flat and editorial brands with square images. Portraits, names and roles are placeholders: use real team photos and names, with permission.

name: founder-note
title: Team / a note from the founder
description: A letter on the surface colour: on the left one arch-topped portrait with the name and role under it; on the right a small eyebrow, a heading, three short paragraphs in the display font and a sign-off line; the portrait goes above the letter on phones.
when: An about page, or a personal touch before the offer, for owner-led businesses (coaches, makers, family firms, studios); warm, friendly and rounded brands. The portrait, name, role and every line of the letter are placeholders for the founder's own words.

name: values-list
title: Values / a numbered manifesto on an inverted band
description: A band in inverted colours (the text colour as the fill): a small eyebrow and heading, then four values as ruled lines, each a small number, the value in very large type and one short line beside it; on phones each value stacks as number, value and line.
when: An about page or the middle of a home page, when the business wants to say what it stands for in a few words (studios, agencies, non-profits, makers); every kind of brand. The four values and their lines are placeholders for the owner's own values.

name: faq-accordion
title: FAQ / accordion of questions
description: A centred intro over a narrow column (up to 800px) of six questions as accordion items filled with the surface colour, one open at a time (the first open), then a centred line pointing to contact. Divi's accordion draws no icon on the open item (it has no open-icon setting).
when: Objection handling before the final call to action, for any business with recurring questions (price, timing, process, guarantees); suits most looks, since the style kit sets the items' frame and corners. Questions and answers are placeholders: answer only what the owner can confirm.

name: faq-two-column
title: FAQ / questions and answers in two columns
description: A split intro (heading and line left, a contact line and a secondary button right) over two columns of open questions and answers set as plain text, each pair under a rule; nothing to click; one column on phones.
when: Objection handling when the answers are short and should be seen without clicking (local services, shops, events, clinics); calm, flat and editorial brands. Questions, answers and the contact line are placeholders for the owner's real answers.

name: faq-toggle-list
title: FAQ / ruled list of large questions
description: A left-aligned intro and a full-width ruled list of five questions set large in the display font, each a toggle that opens on its own (the first open), with no boxes, only a rule under each; a small contact line at the end.
when: Objection handling for brands that like big type and plain lists (studios, consultancies, software, upscale services); square, flat and editorial looks. Questions and answers are placeholders for the owner's real answers.

name: story-timeline
title: Story / milestones across a photo
description: A photo band under a dark scrim: a left-aligned eyebrow, heading and line, then four milestones side by side, each under a light rule: a large year, a short title and one line; two by two on tablets, one column on phones.
when: An about page or a brand story with a few dated turning points (founding, first shop, a move, a new service); every kind of brand. Needs one photo; every year, title and line is a placeholder for the owner's real history (never invented dates).

name: cta-band
title: Call to action / one strong line and a button
description: A full-width band in the accent colour: one large headline on the left and, on the right, a single button with a small optional note under it; on one line on wide screens, the button drops under the headline on narrower screens.
when: The closing call to action of a page, or between long sections, for any offer with one clear next step; calm, flat and editorial brands. The headline and button label are placeholders for the owner's real offer.

name: cta-split-form
title: Call to action / text beside a short form
description: A split on the surface colour: on the left an eyebrow, a heading, one line and three ticked points; on the right a card on the page colour holding a short Divi contact form (name and email) and its button; one column on tablets and phones.
when: Lead capture for a guide, a consultation, a quote or a waiting list (software, services, coaches); modern and dark-glass brands. The points, the line and the button label are placeholders; the form sends to the site admin email (Divi's default) until the owner sets a receiver.

name: cta-card-over-image
title: Call to action / a card on a photo
description: A full-bleed photo band with no scrim: a card on the surface colour sits on the left of the photo and holds an eyebrow, a heading, one line, a rule and a button; the card takes the full width on phones.
when: A closing call to action with a mood photo (a place, a product, a team at work): bookings, visits, enquiries; flat and upscale brands. The pack picture is an illustration: swap it for a real photo of the owner's place, product or team. The copy and button label are placeholders.

name: cta-countdown
title: Call to action / an offer with a countdown
description: A centred intro, a rounded countdown timer on the surface colour (days, hours, minutes and seconds to an end date), then one button. The end date is a far-future placeholder (31 December 2099) so the timer counts; Divi dims every unit that reaches zero.
when: Only for a real, dated deadline the owner confirms (an event, an enrolment window, a launch); modern, rounded and dark-glass brands. The end date is a placeholder (31 December 2099): set the real date and time, and remove the section when the offer ends. Never invent urgency.

name: gallery-masonry-style
title: Gallery / images of uneven heights in three columns
description: A split intro (heading left, one line right) over three columns of square-cornered images in two heights (portrait and landscape crops in alternating order), so the columns read as a staggered wall; one column on phones.
when: A portfolio, venue, product or project gallery with six or more pictures; calm, flat and editorial brands with square images. The images and their alt texts are placeholders: use the owner's own photos.

name: portfolio-featured-grid
title: Portfolio / one featured project over a grid
description: A heading with a secondary button beside it, then a two-column grid of project images: the first project spans both columns, four more sit two by two; each has its name and a small category label under the picture; one column on phones. A static grid: nothing filters.
when: A studio, agency or freelancer portfolio, or case studies, with five projects to show; modern, rounded and dark-glass brands. Project names, categories and images are placeholders for the owner's real work, shown with the client's permission.

name: before-after-compare
title: Gallery / before and after slider
description: A split: on the left an eyebrow, a heading, one line and two short labelled notes (what it was, what changed); on the right Divi's before/after image module, two pictures under one draggable handle; the text goes above the slider on phones.
when: Renovation, cleaning, design, retouching or coaching results where one picture pair says more than words; brands with square images. Both pictures are placeholders: use the owner's own before and after photos of the same view, never staged or borrowed ones.

name: contact-location-form
title: Contact / the place, its address and a form
description: A split on the page colour: on the left an arch-topped photo of the place and, under it, the address and opening hours with icons; on the right a heading, one line and a card on the surface colour with a Divi contact form (name, email, message); the form goes under the place on tablets and phones. No map: Divi's map needs a Google API key and loads a third-party script.
when: A contact page for a business people visit (shop, studio, clinic, cafe); warm and friendly brands. Needs one photo of the place; the address, hours and copy are placeholders: use the owner's real details only. The form sends to the site admin email (Divi's default) until the owner sets a receiver.

name: contact-details-form
title: Contact / ruled details beside a form
description: A left column with an eyebrow, a heading and four ruled contact details (email, phone, address, hours), each an icon, a small label and a placeholder value; a right column with a Divi contact form (name, email, message) on the surface colour; the form goes under the details on tablets and phones.
when: The contact page or the last section of a service page (firms, agencies, trades, clinics); calm, flat and editorial brands. Every email, phone number, address and hour is a placeholder: use the owner's real details only, never invented ones. The form sends to the site admin email (Divi's default) until the owner sets a receiver.

name: transition-wave-band
title: Transition / an inverted band with wave edges
description: A short band in inverted colours (the text colour as the fill) with a wave cut into its top and bottom edges, both waves filled with the page colour so the band seems to flow out of the section above and into the one below; it holds one centred line.
when: Between two sections on the page colour, to break a long page or hand over from one topic to the next (a mission line, a short promise the owner can stand behind, a pointer to what follows); soft, rounded and playful brands. Put it between sections whose background is the page colour; the line is a placeholder.

name: transition-overlap-panel
title: Transition / a card overlapping the edge of a dark band
description: A full-width dark band (the text colour as the fill) with a centred eyebrow, heading and line, then one wide card on the surface colour that is pulled up over the band's lower edge, so it sits half on the band and half on the page colour; the card holds three short points in a row (one column on phones).
when: After a hero or an image-led section, to lead into the detail with depth; soft and layered brands. Follow it with a section on the page colour (the card sits half on the band, half on that colour). The heading, line and points are placeholders.
